a.xlink:title:
Run the requirement simulators of a scenario config: for each instrument, one OpticalTrain, with the DIT shortened if needed so the raw readout (aperture fully open) peaks at <= MAX_RAW_FRAC of saturation (limit_dit_to_saturation); for each requirement with simulate: true that applies to it, the requirement's simulator, simulator(ctx, req_key, req_cfg) -> list of written files, with req_cfg resolved for the instrument's detector (see resolve_for_detector).
INPUTS: - scenario (dict): the scenario config - simulators (dict): requirement key -> simulator function - observing (dict): merged observing config (common + test-specific) - out_dir (str): directory to write to - test_prefix (str): file name prefix, e.g. 'IMG_OPT_04' - plot_dir (str or None): directory for FYI plots (ctx.plot_dir), if any; see sim_plot_dir
OUTPUTS: - dict: (requirement key, instrument name) -> list of written files

Load the common observing config, then merge each test-specific config on top, in order (top-level keys of later files override earlier ones).
INPUTS ---------- stem : str Project root (METIS_MAIT_code_eckhart/), prepended to relative paths. *test_config_files : str Test-specific observing configs, relative to stem or absolute.
OUTPUTS ------- dict The merged observing config.

Load a YAML configuration file and pipe its contents to the log.
INPUTS ---------- config_file_choice : str Path to the configuration file. print_one_line : bool, optional If True, log the entire config on a single line. If False (default), log in a more readable, multiline format.
OUTPUTS ------- config_this : dict The configuration dictionary loaded from file.

pipe its contents to the log

a.xlink:title:
Lower the Strehl ratio of the PSFs in signal by strehl_factor (<= 1), conserving the flux: signal' = s * signal + (1 - s) * halo, with halo = signal convolved with a normalised Gaussian of sigma halo_sigma_pix, and s chosen so that the brightest PSF's peak is strehl_factor times what it was (the others' approximately so).
OUTPUTS: - ndarray: signal' - float: s
a.text: Lower the Strehl ratio of the PSFs

a.xlink:title:
Check the cases of a requirement: a 'pass' and a 'fail' case exist, every case injects every limited quantity, and the 'pass'/'fail' cases are on the right side of the limit. Exits otherwise.
OUTPUTS: - dict: case name -> EXPECTED ('PASS' or 'FAIL')

a.xlink:title: Saturation level (ADU per DIT) from the observing config, or None: that of obs_mode in saturation_adu_by_obs_mode (modes whose detector readout mode differs from the imaging default, e.g. the LSS modes), else that of the detector in saturation_adu.
Detector key ('img_lm' or 'img_n') of a WCU imaging obs_mode.

Shorten the DIT, if needed, so that the peak of the raw readout (aperture fully open) is <= max_frac * saturation_adu. Never lengthens it.
Each trial takes a dark and an illuminated readout at the current DIT. If the raw peak is too high, the DIT is rescaled to aim at target_frac * saturation, assuming the signal is linear in DIT on top of the dark level: dit_new = dit * (target_frac * sat - median(dark)) / (peak - median(dark)), at most halving the DIT per trial if the peak is at saturation (the readout may be clipped there, which makes the linear estimate too optimistic). The readouts are per DIT (ScopeSim averages over NDIT), so NDIT is left as it is; the trials use trial_ndit (default 1: quick, and the noisier peak errs on the safe side; None for the configured NDIT).
INPUTS: - metis: OpticalTrain - instrument (dict): instrument config, with 'dit' and 'ndit' (not modified) - saturation_adu (float): saturation level (ADU per DIT) - max_frac, target_frac (float): limit and aim for the raw peak, as fractions of saturation - max_iter (int): maximum number of trials - readout_fn: readout function, readout_fn(metis, bb_aperture, instrument) -> (frame, header); injectable for tests - trial_ndit (int or None): NDIT of the trial readouts
OUTPUTS: - dict: a copy of instrument with 'dit' set to the tuned DIT - dict: dit_cfg, dit, peak_frac (raw peak / saturation of the last trial), n_trials
Raises ValueError if the dark level alone is >= target_frac * saturation, and RuntimeError if no DIT within max_iter trials is short enough.

a.xlink:title: What a requirement simulator needs for one instrument set-up: the OpticalTrain, the instrument config (DIT already tuned), the merged observing config, the detector saturation level, where and how to write (incl. an optional directory for FYI plots), and (cached, so requirements simulated for the same instrument share them) two independent darks and a full-aperture illuminated frame.
